transcript.text: The sides of our new fridge freezer get really warm, almost hot, especially near the front edge. Is that a fire risk? It's in an alcove between two units.

No, warm sides are not a fire risk. On most modern fridge-freezers, the cooling coils (condensers) are built into the side panels to save space. However, because yours is in an alcove, we need to ensure there is enough airflow. If the unit is pressed tight against the sides, heat can build up and make it run too hard. Please check if there is at least a 5cm gap around the sides and top for air to circulate. Also, does the compressor (the motor you might hear humming at the back) stop and start normally, or does it run non-stop without ever pausing?
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.

The gap is only about 1cm each side, and a few cm above where there's a cupboard. The hum sounds normal to me, but I can't tell if it ever stops. There's no burning smell or scorch marks, and nothing has tripped. Is that gap too small?

Yes, 1cm is too small. The manufacturer usually requires at least 5cm of clear space on all sides and the top for air to circulate properly. Without this gap, the heat from the cooling coils gets trapped, making the sides very hot and forcing the compressor to work harder than it should. To check if your specific model has any known issues or warranty coverage for this installation style, could you please tell me the brand and the full model number? It is usually on a sticker inside the fridge, often near the salad drawer.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
It's a Hotpoint, model H7X 93T SK. I've got the manual here. Should I be worried about it being that hot with such a small gap?

Yes, you should be concerned about that level of heat because 1cm is far too small a gap. The manufacturer typically requires at least 5cm (2 inches) of clearance on all sides and the top to allow air to circulate around the condenser coils built into the panels. Without this space, the heat gets trapped, making the sides dangerously hot and forcing the compressor to work much harder than it should, which can shorten its life. Please move the unit out so there is at least a 5cm gap on all sides and above it. Leave it running with the doors shut for a few hours, then check if the sides are still excessively hot. If they cool down significantly after moving it, the issue was purely the lack of airflow.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.

I'd rather not pull it out, we've just had the new floor laid and I'm worried about scratching it. Is there another way to get the gap right, or something else I can check from the front? The sides are warm like a radiator on low, I can keep my hand on them.

If moving it isn't an option right now due to your new floor, there is no 'front-only' fix for the heat on the sides because the cooling coils are built into those panels. The only way to reduce that heat without moving the unit is to improve airflow around it (e.g., using a small fan to blow air past the sides) or ensure the room isn't too hot. To help me assess if this is purely an installation issue or something else, could you tell me: 1. What is the approximate room temperature where it's installed? 2. Have you put a lot of warm food into it recently, or left the doors open for long periods?
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.

I'm not sure of the exact room temperature, but the kitchen does get warm in summer. I haven't left the doors open for long, but the sides are always warm, a bit more on hot days or after I've loaded lots of food in. Fridge is 4C and freezer -18C, so it's cooling well.

Since the fridge is maintaining 4°C and the freezer -18°C, there is no fault with the cooling system. The warmth you are feeling on the sides is normal: it is heat being removed from inside the appliance and dissipated through those side panels. However, because your unit is in an alcove with only a 1cm gap, that heat cannot escape efficiently into the room. This causes the sides to get much hotter than they would be if there were proper airflow (the recommended 5cm). While this isn't a fire risk right now, it forces the compressor to work harder and use more electricity. To manage this without moving the fridge: try placing a small fan nearby to blow air across the sides of the unit. This will help dissipate the heat and keep the sides cooler. If you can eventually create a bit more space (even just 2-3cm) by adjusting the surrounding units, that would also help significantly.
